levels.title: Chart rank inside each genre
levels.task: Stellar Sound wants ranks inside each genre on the chart. Show track_name, genre, weeks_on_chart, and chart_rank using RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY genre ORDER BY weeks_on_chart DESC). Sort the answer by genre A–Z, then chart_rank small to large, then track_name A–Z. This site checks column order and row order.
levels.initialCode: -- RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY genre ORDER BY weeks_on_chart DESC) AS chart_rank
levels.solution:
SELECT track_name, genre, weeks_on_chart,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY genre ORDER BY weeks_on_chart DESC) AS chart_rank
FROM top_songs
ORDER BY genre, chart_rank, track_name;
levels.hintMessage: Name the window column chart_rank. Final ORDER BY genre, chart_rank, track_name (all going up, no DESC on those three).
levels.successMessage: Great! Ranks restart inside each genre—useful for charts and show lineups.

levels.title: Show order at the summer festival
levels.task: Stellar Sound is also running a summer festival. From festival_performances, show artist_name, set_time, and slot_number = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY set_time). Sort the final list by slot_number from 1 up.
levels.initialCode: -- ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY set_time) AS slot_number
levels.solution:
SELECT artist_name, set_time,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY set_time) AS slot_number
FROM festival_performances
ORDER BY slot_number;
levels.hintMessage: Column order: artist_name, set_time, slot_number. ORDER BY slot_number ascending.
levels.successMessage: Nice! The crew can see who plays in what order.

levels.title: Same total on every festival row
levels.task: Still for the festival table: on every line, show artist_name and total_performances = COUNT(*) OVER () with empty (). That repeats the full count of shows. Sort by artist_name A–Z.
levels.solution:
SELECT artist_name,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_performances
FROM festival_performances
ORDER BY artist_name;
levels.hintMessage: Name the column total_performances. Use COUNT(*) OVER () with nothing between the parentheses.
levels.successMessage: Great! The same total appears on each row so readers do not scroll to count.

levels.title: Running count through the night
levels.task: For the festival schedule, show artist_name, set_time, and running_count = COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY set_time ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW). Copy the OVER part carefully. Sort by set_time only.
levels.initialCode: -- COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY set_time ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
levels.solution:
SELECT artist_name, set_time,
  COUNT(*) OVER (
    ORDER BY set_time
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS running_count
FROM festival_performances
ORDER BY set_time;
levels.hintMessage: Name it running_count. The long ROWS BETWEEN... part must match the answer. ORDER BY set_time.
levels.successMessage: Good! The count grows each time another act starts.

levels.title: Compare each room to the next bigger one
levels.task: Stellar Sound is checking room sizes. From venues, show name, capacity, and previous_capacity = LAG(capacity) OVER (ORDER BY capacity DESC). Sort by capacity high to low, then name A–Z.
levels.initialCode: -- LAG(capacity) OVER (ORDER BY capacity DESC) AS previous_capacity
levels.solution:
SELECT name, capacity,
  LAG(capacity) OVER (ORDER BY capacity DESC) AS previous_capacity
FROM venues
ORDER BY capacity DESC, name;
levels.hintMessage: LAG uses ORDER BY capacity DESC inside OVER. Outside, ORDER BY capacity DESC, name.
levels.successMessage: Great! LAG shows the size of the next bigger room in the sorted list.
